item.title: Listening to off the map i found out im sorta subconsciously expecting the next section (starting at the faster tempo part) to be a repeat of another previous one. but it just Keeps Going n throws something new every danc time. is this intentional. or how much of the next verses have similar parts that im not picking up?? there must be some magic that keeps tricking me it's great
item.description:
6.1.26 3:48 am
Q: Listening to off the map i found out im sorta subconsciously expecting the next section (starting at the faster tempo part) to be a repeat of another previous one. but it just Keeps Going n throws something new every danc time. is this intentional. or how much of the next verses have similar parts that im not picking up?? there must be some magic that keeps tricking me it's great
A: "is this intentional?" when songwriting you really cant plan how it's gonna go, and if you do it gets very stifled. but i certainly dont mind that it does that. if you think "it's great" then i see nothing wrong here. i also must have thought it was good at some point too, because i kept it that way. Although, i would argue that what this song seems to do a lot, is refer back to words that have been used before, at the very least a couple seconds ago. Then there is one fairly big callback reference when it goes to "on the map". At that point, probably what happened is, the songwriter (me) started to realize, oh jeez this really has been very escapist (as you said), so i probably made a concentrated effort right there to recall at least what the name of the song was, and do something with that. in fact i believe i tried to also reflect that situation in the video at that point

item.title: what do you do when you make a deadline for yourself to finish a project and you miss it? and what should i do besides feel dread because no amount of dread has seemed to help yet
item.description:
6.2.26 2:51 pm
Q: what do you do when you make a deadline for yourself to finish a project and you miss it? and what should i do besides feel dread because no amount of dread has seemed to help yet
A: probably everyone's different, but for me when i miss a self imposed deadline, there's nothing else i can do. it's going to take an insanely long time after that. for me there's no such thing as a secondary deadline, or second chance for a deadline. i basically have to wait long enough until i've totally forgotten about the previous failure. i have to wait long enough so that it's the first time again. also, really the only way to get deadlines to work is if i have a whole fixed scheme of deadlines that i have every reason to believe in wholeheartedly. just 1 deadline for 1 thing usually isnt enough

item.title: When you're editing your video and you have to keep replaying one second over and over again, does this ever make you notice something you want to change about the song? And do you change it?
item.description:
6.2.26 7:27 pm
Q: When you're editing your video and you have to keep replaying one second over and over again, does this ever make you notice something you want to change about the song? And do you change it?
A: i had a whole answer for this but then i realized your question is different from what i thought. Normally i would say hearing the same part over and over is a one way ticket to terrible judgement. But in this case, i think you're talking about when the song is done and youre working on the video. In that case, generally, judgement about the song will be better than ever because your main worry would be the video. so yes, sometimes the during the video editing is the best time to have better judgement about the song. as uncomfortable as it may be to have to go back into an already 'done' song, sometimes it can be all too clear when doing the video that there is 1 little thing that really does need to be fixed

item.title: if you had infinite money, that means infinte tax. would you then have 0 money? ∞ - ∞ = 0, right?
item.description:
6.4.26 5:49 am
Q: if you had infinite money, that means infinte tax. would you then have 0 money? ∞ - ∞ = 0, right?
A: this is where 'different infinities' arises. tax is supposed to be less than 100%. less than 100% an infinite value has to be something conceptually less than the first value. even if both values are infinite. in this case, after tax you'd still be left with infinite, which would be conceptually smaller than what you had initially. The way this might play out: you have infinite money in the long term, but whatever amount you spend each day has a certain percentage of it going to whomever is taxing you. you still have infinite more, and the tax collector still gets an unlimited stream

A: i didn't exactly say that, but what i would say is, to translate a song not just to translate, but to also re-write. In your case, you may wish to add a restriction that the melody must stay the same. this creates an interesting challenge. and again, to pull it off gracefully takes songwriting, not just translation. On some level, in fact, any kind of translation, whether it's dialogue or a novel or something else, to get a good result, requires a certain amount of writing and re-imagining to make it work right, and there are always a number of bizarre challenges to solve. but the extreme case of this would be with songs

item.description:
6.7.26 6:39 pm
Q: I've kinda sucked at writing lyrics for as long as i can remember writing lyrics for my songs, which might have something to do with the fact that when im listening to music im listening to the tones and the melodies etc more than the lyrics; i hear/my brain prioritises non-voice over voice in a song when listening usually. Any advice to get better at it? I've been trying to write small to medium sized stories and poems as of late too to see if maybe that could help (and ofcourse yk, trying to listen to song lyrics more carefully every now and then). Thnx!
A: you're gonna have to find out what YOU wanna say. Because perhaps you've "listened" to other people's "words" a little "less" than perhaps "most people" do, that might perhaps mean that your lyrical voice might turn out to be a bit "different" than other people's. So that means two things: it means if you try to sort of half-heartedly "imitate" what "other people" do lyrically, it will sound fake and it wont really move anyone, but it also means that if you put in the time to explore deep within yourself to find out what YOU actually want to say, ..... it may be surprising to you and everyone, how wild it is. people will be impressed and wonder what the heck planet you got it from. the only thing is, you have to put in the time to make the long and personal journey to whatever planet YOU personally connect with. it probably wont happen over night, but, trust me, it's the most fun and fulfilling thing you could ever imagine

Q: which colour do you think is the most trustworthy? which is the least trustworthy?
A: it's not individual colors, but combinations of colors. pairs of colors that are the most reliable are pairs with extreme differences in brightness. for example, black and white. pairs that are the least reliable are colors with the exact same level of brightness, which may look the same as each other when viewed by a colorblind person or device, and any designs or writing done in this scheme would be illegible

item.title: I find it interesting that "i get turned on by the news" was written to mean "it is normal to get freaked out by the news because that's literally its job", I had always interpreted it as enjoying the news such that the person watching is complacent in whatever the news is talking about
item.description:

A: keep in mind, the previous line was "turn on the news", so the fact that i use the phrase "turned on" was a bit of wordplay to match the previous line (it is a song after all). but indeed it is referring to the news's intended role of getting our attention by agitating us. if you watch the video for the song it may be a little more clear: there are flames on the screen. further playing into the trope that the news always tries their very best to find flames to show you, if they can. ah, now i remember, the next line also continues to explain this "the news gets more views whenever there's cool news", 'cool' in this case being a bit of a euphamism for..... attention getting, horrifying, etc

item.title: How did you find your dogma with your very specific sounds and arranging-style?
item.description:
6.15.26 6:30 pm
Q: How did you find your dogma with your very specific sounds and arranging-style?
A: just living my life and being who i am, led me to the decisions i've made. mind you, we are almost certainly headed toward some gargantuan philosophical revolutions with regard to just about all the various technologies most of us have adopted and accepted in music as commonlplace, over the past 50 years or so. there has perhaps never been a better time to ditch many of those. some of which i never used anyway, but i will surely be having a think, to see what ways i can take a healthy step backward on the technological progression trajectory, back toward the human side of the spectrum. that being said, i have to strike a balance because my methods work extremely well for me so if i change too much it will be more of a setback than an advantage. but i think it's prime time to second guess even some of the most basic technological advancements we've all been using for decades. the thirst for realness is about to become overwhelming

item.description:
6.15.26 7:19 pm
Q: Bill, I really appreciate your extremely anti-AI sentiments which are strongly hinted at in your responses, not that I am surprised that an artist like yourself has such feelings about the tech being applied to art. In one question recently, you seemed to imply "off the map" was through composed because that seems less likely to be ai generated. Do you actually feel like you need to make some extra effort to prove your work is genuine? I hope you don't but i also understand and empathize with an incapability to not think about AI constantly these days. Here's to hoping it takes up less headspace in yours than mine (I work in tech). Thanks for all the brilliant work you've produced over the years. Your work has always been inspiring and incredibly moving.
A: "off the map" was already fully written in 2023, so i can't say that that's specifically the reason that it is the way it is. but it's always nice to try to step back and realize "slop" is not new. the mission of creativity is always to find new ways to prove we're alive. slop used to be made by hardworking uncreative people, now thankfully we can all more fully devote to genuine creativity. "verse chorus" is fine and great, and i have many songs written that use that. but i've always taken every opportunity to take the creative approach. for example, starting about 25 years ago we all started to notice it may be commonplace to actually copy the recording of the first chorus vocals to the second chorus. I mean, that's just a perfectly wasted opportunity. even if you only just change 1 word, change 1 little thing, that gives the audience a sign at least that you're there! that you haven't left the building and left the song on auto-play. so this is not really a new concept. so just as almost like a religion, i never copy vocals from 1 section to another, or even any instrumental parts. Like a mother to a child, i want to be there for you. you need to know i'm there. because, when i am on the listening side of things, when i'm the listener and you're the artist, i need to know you're there. that's what it all comes down to, at any point in our technological history. that's the core issue the audience needs to know: "are you really there?" and as artists, it's our job to prove we're really there. and as time goes by and the technology does this or that, the methods for proving you're really there will always have to change. that's what makes it so much fun. as everything changes, the core issue, and in fact the ONLY issue that ever remains constant is, "are you really there?" by the way, there's also no reason you cant use ai in all kinds of ways and still prove youre there. but it's too soon to see exactly how that plays out, and the audience needs time to get used to sorting it all out and knowing the difference. plus, as usual i tend not to get into big new technologies until maybe 10 years after the fact. so we'll see. but the miracle of all this, as always, is that it further clarifies our understanding of just what means something to us and what does not

item.title: You know I'm very confused by you. You'll make references to my existence in your work, seemingly wanting my attention to communicate, yet whenever I reach out to you directly, you never actually seem to respond. Why is that? Do you think hiding our past in your music is a genuine replacement for addressing me? Do you have any idea how frustrating it is to see you write me into your fictitious world, all the while giving me NO WAY to have a private conversation with you? What exactly do you want here? In the past when I wrote you letters, you ignored me. When I couldn't take it anymore and left to move on, you use the map thing to call me back???? The nuance and liberty of using your life experience as inspiration is not lost on me. But you and I know full well that's not what you're trying to do. You're using this as a replacement for communication! Hiding behind fear! Just.. relentlessly teasing my existence to me. You make me feel like a ghost! Never,ever allowed to have any kind of meaningful or tangible moments! All these years I thought I had a delusion, thinking I was over stepping boundaries and misinterpreting things! Yet it turns out you really were egging me on the whole time! I know it took a lot for you to post again And I'm so proud of you for overcoming your fear. I'll never understand why you're so hard on yourself. Or why you keep holding yourself back. Truly the only thing keeping you in your personal prison is yourself Bill. I wish you would understand you've had the keys to freedom in your hand the entire time. Since im absolutely abusing this box for it's intended purpose, and have no intention of doing this ever again, Im going to just get everything off my chest. And I truly can't go on living like this anymore. (After all, emailing you didn't work, just like I thought it wouldn't.) Im sorry for coming and going as much as I did. I tried my best to encourage you anonymously from a distance. Because honestly. You've always kept me at a distance. It was the only way I could muster a reason to say any thing to you at all. I figured so long as you heard my thoughts, they didn't need to come from "me". I'm sorry if that upset you. I know it wasn't an honest thing to do. I know I was being cowardly because I felt like my pride was hurt. And I know it was especially unfair to you when I knew my silence harmed you. I was not fair to you for me to leave and never properly communicate after. I'm sorry for making you think I didn't care about you or how you were doing when I really did. But I wish you would understand how upsetting it is writing all this, knowing I'll never get any kind of closure from you. A proper conversation about what all of this was It was really, truly the only thing I ever wanted from you. So I guess this is me giving it to myself. I can't and won't play these games with you anymore Bill. Stop asking me to play with you.

A: at the risk of stating the painfully obvious, you and i have never met. yes, you are absolutely delusional. that's ok, it's not a crime to have these kinds of thoughts and feelings, and in fact it's very common. heck, there's movies about this. the classic condition when a person thinks they are receiving personalized messages through the television, except in this case you feel like you are getting messages through my songs and videos. this is not new, and you're certainly not the only person who has suffered from this exact sort of delusion, relating to my work. as a matter of fact, even if i were to look in my inbox right now to find your messages, i wouldnt even be able to tell which one is you because there are so many different people with this same condition. i feel i am bursting an enormous bubble here, and it's also very much not my place to get involved with this, because i am not a professional psychologist or psychiatrist. and i also realize how triggering and rude it would seem to simply say "you need help", which, quite simply, you very much do. and it wouldn't exactly be helpful if i didn't also suggest where to find help. which unfortunately i can't do. so basically i'm sorry for not knowing where the help is going to come from. i am a music and video artist, making creative works. you have evidently been swept away by the content so intensely that you literally think the songs are about you. they are not about you specifically, they are about anyone who may be moved by them. this is standard artistic practice. this is how art works. and again, it is unfortunately quite common for people to find themselves in the mental state that you are in. what you are dealing with is far beyond my level of psychiatric professionalism (which is technically zero), so the safest thing for both of us is certainly for me not to respond at all. but you seem like you are suffering a great deal and it just feels like you need a friendly reminder that i am an artist and you and i have never met. my music and videos are not written about you, because i don't know anything about you. and you are also not the only person who thinks they are specifically about them. to do great art, you wanna sweep the audience away, but the risk here of course is that some segments of the audience can be so prone to being swept away that they get swept a little too far. i am sorry about this

item.title: are the neighbors you're wondering about in "i'm a princess" supposed to represent your listening audience (i know everyone's free to interpret the lyrics however they want to but like... did you have that in mind when you were writing that part?)
item.description:
6.19.26 10:28 am
Q: are the neighbors you're wondering about in "i'm a princess" supposed to represent your listening audience (i know everyone's free to interpret the lyrics however they want to but like... did you have that in mind when you were writing that part?)
A: that is not what i had in mind. it's hard to describe exactly what's on the mind in songwriting, which is why we have to turn to music to express it, but here's one way of seeing what's happening here: it's basically the second verse (because we've come back and repeated the starting title line). so the second time around, we expand the perspective outward a notch. to the next house over, let's say. Even if they are not there, conceptually this is where the mind goes at first. often, the 'second verse' goes somewhere like 'the next day' or something, but the feeling so far in this song is a feeling of sort of dreary eternity, like days dont exist. so in the abscense of time, we turn to space, and the concept of neighbors. which, probably as i realized immediately after saying the word neighbors, probably wouldnt be there in this song. i'm just mondaymorningquarterbacking (no pun intended) how this may have happened, in the songwriting session in 2019 because i dont entirely remember. but the line feels right to me now, and it must have also felt right to me then, so i have every reason to believe that the line felt the same way to me then as how i've described it now

item.title: hello i think you do linguistic stuff (????) im confident enough to speak 3 languages (english, finnish, swedish) and im currently learning 3 more (german, spanish, japanese) as well as russian (starting next school year) do you have advice for keeping up with so many got dang languages at once i think youre qualified for this right? right????
item.description:
6.21.26 3:47 pm
Q: hello i think you do linguistic stuff (????) im confident enough to speak 3 languages (english, finnish, swedish) and im currently learning 3 more (german, spanish, japanese) as well as russian (starting next school year) do you have advice for keeping up with so many got dang languages at once i think youre qualified for this right? right????
A: i'm not exactly qualified for this question. why: because i can hardly claim to have even reached fluency in a second language. despite listening and immersing intensely for multiple years in the dutch language (nederlands), by my standards i would not consider myself fluent, although i'm close. my next best language would be french, in which i had a standard highschool level second-language education (which absolutely did NOT amount to any kind of fluency) and then in recent years i've begun to give it the same treatment i've given to dutch, but i've only accumulated about 20% as much time with it, and i've made more progress than i ever did in school, but i am still nowhere near fluent comprehension. Additionally, there was a period of time where i got into multiple languages, like you, but i could not curb my greed, and my wishlist of languages had 20 languages on it. I did spend quite a lot of time in each one of those languages, and increased my familiarity with each one of them, but in most of those i am lightyears away from any kind of comprehension. and it's possible that a multilanguage approach, even if i could limit it to 4 or so, might not be feasible at all. i still bounce around between dutch french and spanish, and sometimes i think i'm ruining my chances of success in any of them, just because the time is so divided. so i have no idea what i'm doing

item.title: you say you get ideas for your songs at unexpected moments. in that case, how do you retain them in your mind for long enough such that you can later write them down or record them to get back to them later? a lot of really cool songs i've invented have never come to be because I'm unable to remember them for long enough before I can play them, and it's very frustrating
item.description:
6.24.26 8:13 am
Q: you say you get ideas for your songs at unexpected moments. in that case, how do you retain them in your mind for long enough such that you can later write them down or record them to get back to them later? a lot of really cool songs i've invented have never come to be because I'm unable to remember them for long enough before I can play them, and it's very frustrating
A: if you really wanna catch it, you gotta catch it right when you get it. there's plenty of devices that can record your voice, most commonly a phone or something. if you cant speak into your phone, there are ways of writing it on paper if you have paper (notation systems, numbering systems, etc), but more likely you may only have access to text, such as on a touch screen on your phone, which is much less ideal, but if you can fight against the autocorrect you can write down some descriptions, melody rhythm and chord indications, and describe as specifically as you can what you're hearing. Now, .... if you don't have any way to accurately describe music to yourself, describe rhythms, describe melodies, etc, then that's something you'll need to develop. you can borrow from the notation systems that are widely in use, or you can make your own system that caters best to your needs. but one way or another you're going to need a way to communicate with yourself. for example, a carpenter probably has names for their tools, even if they made up their own names

item.title: I'm going to be doing my first real live performance in a week or so (the first one with more than about 30 people watching at least) Any advice you can offer on having a good stage presence? Most of what I've done so far is just smile where I can and move around a little but I feel like that might not cut it
item.description:
6.25.26 4:01 am
Q: I'm going to be doing my first real live performance in a week or so (the first one with more than about 30 people watching at least) Any advice you can offer on having a good stage presence? Most of what I've done so far is just smile where I can and move around a little but I feel like that might not cut it
A: the worst thing to do is think about it before you get there. because you dont even know what it is. it will feel different from anything you've ever known. it will take you at least 20 times to really get comfortable with it. basically however many times it takes for you to get used to how crazy it feels. but the one time you should not even try to think or feel anything about it is RIGHT NOW before youre there. you'd be confusing yourself over nothing. i know youre excited, but do something completely different. perform your best now for where you currently are NOW. then when you get THERE, ..... you will be shocked because it will be the first time, and i think it will take maybe 20 shows to get used to it. THEN, youre yourself again, and now people are there with you. it's great, very easy. will not happen the first time. 1st time shocked. so no point in thinking about it right now, do something else to distract. and look forward to the shock, that's pretty much it

item.title: so i just learned that you used a random number generator to decide which song to work on next (like and the day goes on), so does that mean that your recent (post 2020) songs also pull from that same set of old songs? or is it a mix of old and new? do you make an effort to pick the "best" songs?
item.description:
6.28.26 4:29 pm
Q: so i just learned that you used a random number generator to decide which song to work on next (like and the day goes on), so does that mean that your recent (post 2020) songs also pull from that same set of old songs? or is it a mix of old and new? do you make an effort to pick the "best" songs?
A: trying to pick 'the best' usually means playing it way too safe. what you can do, however, is narrow it down to 5 or 10 that are very exciting, then secretly try to beef up each one of them in competition with the others. in other words, go around to each one and say, what would i need to do to this one to make it suddenly crush all the others. and you go around and keep doing that and strenghening all of them and making them fight with each other, until you essentially feel scared NOT to pick every single one of them. then you know you can be safe doing a random, and be assured that the selection is legitimate. Because, once you start production, you can and will begin to feel terrible from time to time, and if there is ANY doubt in the selection, you will fall apart and try to blame the selection. so that is how we ensure confidence in the selection. and so i am collecting from the entire list of everything i have, but i narrow it down to ones that seem the most exciting at that time. then i make them fight with each other, then i end up with 5 or 10 that i absolutely cant imagine NOT picking, then random from those. it's always interesting to look back and see what the other finalists were. for example, when 'soft clothing' got picked, with a different flip of the dice would one of 3 other songs been recorded instead, one of them is actually the one i'm doing now. and all 4 had probably been in the finals before. Sometimes one gets knocked out for awhile, for silly reasons like it collides with another one. for example, the one i'm working on now actually fell out of favor for a while after 'money', and previously also after 'first day of school think i might quit', due to certain surface-level similarities, so you want to let a bit more time pass before appearing to do two songs that maybe reference the same thing somewhere in them, or maybe have certain similar musical attributes such as tempo or time feel. for example there's another one that i really wanted to pick this time, but it has one tiny moment that is kind of a little bit similar to a moment in 'off the map'. so that one will be delayed for a little while but will probably come up again after a few more go by. the one i'm doing now has been around since 2018 (at least the first line was), and another one of the finalists this time was one with about a minute written in 2011 and about 30 more seconds written in 2025, which i expect will be pretty persistent and be selected soon. along with many, many others

item.title: have you ever thought about not doing songs in a language? like, instead of english lyrics, just making sounds that sound good along with the instrumental, basically nonsense words that sound good, do you ever want that kind of freedom?
item.description:
6.30.26 7:33 am
Q: have you ever thought about not doing songs in a language? like, instead of english lyrics, just making sounds that sound good along with the instrumental, basically nonsense words that sound good, do you ever want that kind of freedom?
A: i have precisely this kind of freedom, and then this makes it even more powerful to sometimes use words. this combination is where the magic really happens. i vividly remember the day i realized what a powerful combination this is. "it's as if the worded part explains what the unworded part was about, and in turn the unworded part shows us how we feel about the worded part" is what i realized, and i employ this technique constantly to this day. sometimes the unworded part is caught by an instrument or something, other times i'll vocalize it, often both, but this 'worded - unworded' interplay is is a technique i stick to almost religiously
